title.narrative: Support to TAHA: Growing Wealth Through Horticulture (GROWTH)
Support to TAHA: Growing Wealth Through Horticulture (GROWTH)

description.narrative: Projektets övergripande mål är att öka konkurrenskraft och hållbarhet för hortikultur (trädgårdsodling). Det svenska stödet riktas till den ideella organisationen (TAHA) genom projektet "Growing Wealth through Horticulture" med fokus på: • Öka produktiviteten genom att förbättra kunskap om effektiva och hållbara jordbruksmetoder, med tonvikt på att integrera miljö och klimatförändringar, • Öka tillgången till marknader för tanzaniska hortikultur produkter, • Bidra till opinionsbildning och främjande av en bättre politik och affärsmöjliggörande miljö för hortikulturens konkurrenskraft och delaktighet.

The overall objective (s) of the Project is increasing competitiveness and sustainability of horticultural industry. The Swedish support is directed to the non-profit Association (TAHA) through the project "Growing Wealth through Horticulture" with focus on: • Increasing productivity by improved knowledge on efficient and sustainable farming methods, with emphasis on integrating environment and climate change , • increase access to markets for Tanzanian horticultural products, • Contributing to advocacy for better policy and business enabling environment for horticultural industry's competitiveness and inclusiveness.

description.narrative:
Regarding increasing productivity, there has been a satisfactory result in building capacity on sustainable farming methods. A good number (159, 000) farmers have been trained on sustainable horticultural farming practices which includes environmentally friendly and climate smart agricultural practices which have resulted in increase of productivity for vegetables, fruits and spices of between 2050 percent. For instance, avocado, as an emerging value chain of interest to famers in Tanzania, the production has been increasing at an incredible pace and it might overtake Kenya, the regional leader in coming two or three years. The export of Tanzania horticulture crops by TAHA accredited off-takers including avocadoes is also increasing.
Integration of Environment and climate change mitigation and adaptation: It is reported that TAHA trained more than 17 000 farmers on environmentally sustainable farming methods including integrated pest management (no use of chemical pesticides) and proper pesticide management if needed, economical water use, agroforestry, and other environment sustainability practices. TAHA also trained farmers and extension officer of GLOBALG.A. P certification standards requirements.
In the regreening efforts, TAHA is promoting planting tree crops either fruit, spices, medicinal or ornamental trees. So far two nurseries of 5,900 avocado seedlings are established in Arusha and 45,000 indigenous trees seedlings in are expected to be transplanted in semiarid areas such as Dodoma and some parts of Arusha and Kilimanjaro due to their high resistance to drought.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
